newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Most urban Chinese unaware of life insurance - survey.
newsitem.headline: Most urban Chinese unaware of life insurance - survey.

text.p: Nearly seven out of 10 urban Chinese householders are completely ignorant about life insurance according to a recent survey, market researcher Gallup said on Tuesday.

"There is a very large potential market for life insurance in urban China. However, the market is largely hidden due to a huge lack of information and awareness," the survey, conducted for insurance giant National Mutual Asia Ltd, said.
"Less than one in 10 respondents has life insurance for which they pay 300 yuan (US$36) or more each year," it said.
Sixty-five percent were not even aware of the concept of life insurance.
More than 2,500 interviews were conducted with householders selected randomly.
Over half the respondents were aged between 30 and 39.
Conducted over recent months, the survey covered 50 cities throughout China including the capital Beijing, Shanghai on the eastern seaboard and Guangzhou in the south.
It showed that only 30 percent of urban Chinese respondents were making financial preparations for untimely death.

Vice-president of the U.S.-based Gallup, Richard Burkholder, told a news conference in Hong Kong that urban Chinese consumers were not familiar with how life insurance worked, or aware of specific benefits they might receive.
"Many survey indicators point to a lack of knowledge regarding life insurance, and suggest an enormous need for education in order to develop the market," Burkholder said.
The survey comes as Beijing feels increasing pressure to ease restrictions on foreign insurers wanting to operate in China.
National Mutual is not among the three foreign insurers allowed to operate in China, but said it is hoping to be licensed as market access broadens.
Of China's 1.2 billion people, about 15 percent live in urban areas.
Although life insurance premiums accounted for 30 percent of China's total insurance market, it remained far below the 72 percent average for all of Asia.
